output.brief: Most likely this is one chance QC outlier. The repeat on the same vial passed. The other QC levels and sodium and chloride were fine, and the 1-3s rule is expected to give about one or two chance flags a month. QC means before and after the lot change agree, and all 23 held samples and 20 of the 186 flagged results re-run on Analyzer A agreed within limits. B's patient median is normal, and no QC was skipped. A short sample is possible but unproven, so don't record it as the confirmed cause. Ward 6's high potassiums are split evenly between analyzers A and B. They coincide with the tube outage, long transit times and four renal overflow patients. That points to delayed samples and the patient mix, not analyzer false highs. Nothing has been requested as repeats yet. I did not collect extra evidence. Sign off: return B to service, with extra Level 2 QC for a week as a precaution. Close the 186 flagged results without amendment, and do not recall results, quarantine the lot, or widen limits. Ask Ward 6 for repeat samples on the high results and get the tube repaired. Confidence is moderate, around 65%.
